svg.title: Realtime Speech Interpreter: architecture
svg.desc: Audio leaves the venue mixer, goes through OBS and SRT to a Network Load Balancer and a Fargate app. The app calls Transcribe, Translate or Bedrock, and Polly, then publishes Japanese audio to a LiveKit server on EC2. Listener browsers play the audio. A CloudFront, S3 and Lambda path serves the page and subscribe-only tokens. Secrets Manager and CloudWatch Logs support the pipeline.

g.text: VPC, public subnets in 2 AZs, no NAT
SRT is accepted from the venue IP only
Audio line out from the mixer goes into OBS (or any SRT encoder).
OBS sends SRT with Opus audio over the internet to the load balancer (UDP, venue IP only).
The load balancer passes it to the Fargate app. ffmpeg decodes it to 16 kHz PCM.
The app streams the audio to Transcribe streaming, with language identification.
Transcribe returns text. The app drops non-English results and cuts chunks.
Translate (default) or a Bedrock model (optional, dashed) translates each chunk.
Polly speaks the Japanese text, with readings for product names.
The app publishes the audio to LiveKit over WebRTC (Opus), and the caption text as data packets.
The listener's browser plays the audio and shows the captions from LiveKit (subscribe only).
The browser loads the page from CloudFront and asks for a token.
CloudFront serves the page from a private S3 bucket.
CloudFront calls the token Lambda, which returns a subscribe-only token.
Dashed grey lines: secrets are read from Secrets Manager (app, LiveKit host, token Lambda); app, LiveKit and Lambda logs go to CloudWatch Logs.
